Params: On the dance floor, Nirvatia takes your hand and leads you into a dance.
Her form is impeccable, her every step elegant. She guides you with her every move, letting you spin and unfurl with perfect grace.
Her skirt sweeps a wide arc, the distance between you two always just right. Under Nirvatia's lead, you dance along effortlessly.
Getting me here and testing me at the door was a lot of work.
Surely there's more to it than just a dance?
Tell me, do you recognize this song?
That's right. A waltz, yet its tempo is lento. Elegant, with a quiet sorrow beneath it.
The composer of this song left his homeland over a misunderstanding and never returned.
Are you saying that mirrors your situation?
Is that why you like it?
You misunderstood me. I like it simply because it's beautiful.
With your help, I'll complete the unfinished rite and return to my family.
What makes you think I'd help you?
There is still a case with your name on it.
What if I'm working with the sheriff?
Maybe you should give me a reason not to turn you in first.
The song changes key. Nirvatia follows the melody and glides closer to you, her chin nearly resting on your shoulder.
The fact that you're asking for a reason instead of just turning me in is already reason enough.
I came to you because there's potential for a partnership, and because you have questions only I can answer.
Otherwise, why would your detective board be covered in photos of me?
You know the truth behind the Mist?
Nirvatia presses a finger to your lips, silently signalling you to say no more.
Don't be a killjoy. Help me get what I want, and you'll get what you want.
Remember the first question you asked me?
I didn't go through all this trouble of inviting you here and setting up that little test at the door just to share a dance with you.
The test at the door was to verify your abilities, and you passed in quite a clever manner, I must say.
As for the other matter... The truth of this world isn't something you can simply have just because you want it.
【kuroname】, are you worthy of uncovering such secrets?
Before you can answer, she tilts your chin up, forcing you to meet her crystalline crimson gaze.
A thread of light stirs from somewhere deep within her pupils.
The world tilts. Nirvatia's face fills your vision, every lash, every curve of her smile expanding inch by inch, and your mind is drawn forward as if you are being pulled under by a warm hand.
Deep within your mind, something ancient and long dormant stirs awake.
A thread of golden light rises, shattering the fog that has coiled around your every thought.
So your interest in this goes beyond mere detective's curiosity...
There is a secret within you, too. One that has yet to be unraveled.
This time, it is you who use a spin to draw her closer.
No, I'm just a detective. A perceptive one.
Your hands have gone cold, and you are getting exhausted.
I think using your ability takes something off your life every time.
So the way I see it... you need me far more than I need you.
As the song draws to an end, you take charge with one final spin, your arm locked steady around her shoulders, guiding her into a slow, languid dip.
Every beat before this moment was hers to command, but now, it is your turn.
A flicker of genuine surprise crosses Nirvatia's eyes.
But I'll take the lead from here.
As the song fades out, a smattering of applause rises around you. Perhaps your dance was too beautiful to ignore.
By the champagne tower, a young blonde woman mid-conversation turns at the sound, her gaze drifting toward you.
And a mask like that could never hide eyes as beautiful as yours.
You guide Nirvatia to the edge of the ballroom floor.
Yet the blonde woman's gaze lingers.
Her confusion replaced by disbelief, the blonde woman asks tentatively.
Nirvatia's expression does not change at the familiar voice, but you can feel the hand clasped around yours tightens briefly.
Catching Nirvatia's reaction, the blonde woman sets down her glass and walks toward you.
"Nirvatia" is a forbidden name in the Velosenne household.
The moment her name leaves Jagienka's lips, the ballroom freezes. Music sputters out, glasses stop mid-air, conversations die in an instant... Every eye in the room snaps toward you.
A bullet grazes Nirvatia's hair and buries itself into the column behind her. Stone fragments spray your face.
In the shadow of the second-floor gallery stands an old man in a black coat, the barrel of his gun still trailing white smoke.
The traitor who killed the head of the family!
A lady's scream shatters the silence. Men scramble toward the exits with their heads down, a waiter's tray goes flying, champagne floods the floor... The ballroom erupts into chaos.
Servants close in from all sides.
You grab Nirvatia by the arm and try to disappear into the fleeing crowd.
Nirvatia does not budge. She reaches back and grabs your wrist.
What we came for is somewhere in this house.
We can come back for it!
How do you plan on getting in?
I know the way. Follow me.
Seeing Nirvatia move away, you clench your jaw and run after her toward the inner estate, despite bullets flying from every direction.
They're heading deeper into the estate! The nerve!
After them! She will not leave the Velosenne estate today!
Bullets whistle past your ears. The two of you duck low and dash into the main corridor, rounding a corner and shaking your pursuers... for now.
Eileena catches up to you. Bracing against the wall, she doubles over and gasps for breath.
Nirvatia and you are both startled.
What the?! Why did you follow us here?!
You were being chased! What was I supposed to do?
Shouldn't you have run the other way then?
We're partners! I'm not leaving you behind!
You've been in my room and you don't know my assistant?
Wait a minute... they called her Nirvatia at the ball... Didn't I tell you to hold off on investigating her?!
Hold on—when was she in your room?
A sharp click echoes from the end of the corridor. A shot fires, tearing through the oil painting beside you and splitting the canvas in two, and the frame crashes to the floor.
Nirvatia grabs Eileena by the collar and yanks her out of the path of the stray bullets, then points toward the corner ahead.
The three of you bolt forward, your heads down. But you all freeze the moment you round the corner.
A solid stone wall blocks your path. There are no windows... no way out.
The thud of boots on the floorboards grows louder. You can hear your pursuers' shouts getting closer and closer.
Are you sure this is the right way?
No way... I haven't even cracked a single big case yet... Is my detective career really going to end before it even begins...?
Then, with a soft click, the family portrait on the wall stirs.
The frame splits open to reveal a narrow gap. Through it, Margaret's silver hair peeks out.
Outside, the footsteps and shouting do not let up.
Search every room! They couldn't have gotten far!
Eileena is the last one in. Pressing herself flat against the hidden door, she is terrified of leaving even a crack for someone to spot.
The footsteps outside draw close, then fade into the distance.
Eileena lets out a long breath and sags against the door.
The candlelight flickers. Nirvatia and the silver-haired girl stand across from each other, neither one willing to speak first. Their shadows stretch long against the wall.
You hang back in the shadows, arms crossed, content to watch the drama unfold.
You're finally back. We've been waiting for you.
...What have you done to my room, Margaret?
It does look like a young woman's bedroom.

The spacious and grand outer room was once a parlor. A photo of Nirvatia at 17, taken at a shooting range, hangs on the wall, pristine as the day it was framed. Someone has been keeping this place up.
The door had been replaced with a large picture frame, turning the room into a hidden chamber.
The room just sat empty after you left.
I was worried someone would claim it, so Jagienka and I quietly had it changed.
Not a single thing is missing, and we can change it back by tomorrow.
What just happened must have been a misunderstanding... Jagienka would never order anyone to hurt you.
This ball was even thrown in your honor.
We've held it every year on your birthday since you left. We'd play your favorite waltz, and Jagienka would set your favorite cake on your table, only throwing it out when it had gone bad.
Um... s-sorry, can I just jump in here?
Aren't you two supposed to be... archenemies or something?
No. Jagienka, Nirvatia, and I... we were the closest of friends, once...
Everything makes even less sense to me now.
If you were the closest of friends... who was it that fired on us at the ball just now?
When the head of a family dies, many line up for the inheritance.
One fewer heir means a bigger cut for those old vultures.
With stakes like that, many would be happy to see Nirvatia dead.
Then... why are you still the closest of friends...?
The version I heard painted her as a madwoman who murdered the head of the family and fled...
Clearly, there's more to this story.
Their adoptive father is the one who really deserves to die.
Nirvatia hasn't told them yet, I suppose...
She's always kept everything bottled up inside. I'm happy to know that she has someone she can open up to.
You pieced all of that together in the last five minutes. Nirvatia never said a single word.
You glance over at Nirvatia. She looks back, her eyes full of quiet anticipation.
I won't pry if you don't want to share, and I'm not going to stop you from doing whatever brought you back today. I'll help you.
But when this is all over, you come back and tell us everything from the beginning. Deal?
Nirvatia looks at her for a long moment, then gives a slow, heavy nod.
Right, I still have a mountain of questions rattling around in my head, but...
Eileena clears her throat with exaggerated importance and straightens up.
Since things have already gone this far...
Nirvatia blinks, shooting Eileena a puzzled look.
I'll throw on your veil and bolt down the west staircase. All they'll catch is a silhouette, and they'll come running after me. That's your window to go where you need to go!
You two aren't exactly the same height.
Margaret smiles and lifts the dark veil from Nirvatia's shoulders, draping it over herself.
I'll draw them away. They won't dare touch me.
Do me a favor and find the breaker room on the west side and kill the main switch. They'll be scrambling with the lights out, and that will buy us more time.
Margaret moves to you last, giving you a pat on the shoulder.
You know, Nirvatia might seem cold on the outside, but she's actually really generous and kind-hearted. Just take a little initiative, and I'm sure she'll warm up to you.
Now, I'm leaving her in your hands.
The two of them leave as planned, and only you and Nirvatia are left in the room now.
Nirvatia's expression darkens, as if there are a thousand unspoken words lodged in her throat.
